Witkoff blasted for calling Putin a "humanitarian"
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:57:00 UTC
23:57:00 KST

Witkoff faces backlash for calling Putin a "humanitarian": "Embarrassing and outrageous"
Washington — U.S. special envoy Steve Witkoff faced immediate backlash Wednesday for praising Russian President Vladimir Putin as a "humanitarian" after he released 74-year-old Stephen Hubbard, an American who had been imprisoned in Russia for four years and who had been determined to be wrongfully detained.
"You talk so much about my president, President Trump, being a humanitarian," Witkoff told Putin Wednesday in response to Hubbard's release. "You are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that, I commend you, and I thank you again."
Witkoff made the comment in St. Petersburg during a visit with the Russian president that was aimed at moving toward a resolution of the Ukraine war that Putin started four and a half years ago. Over the past month, Russia has been intensifying its strikes against civilian and energy infrastructure to try to cripple the power grid before the brutal Ukrainian winter.
Mr. Trump was asked later in the day if he would describe Putin the same way Witkoff did. "Well, I guess you have to say for that particular purpose, for the purpose of allowing a man who was thinking he was going to be in prison for life out," Mr. Trump said during a White House roundtable on cyber crime. "But I wouldn't say anything one way or the other."
Witkoff's "humanitarian" comment sparked pushback from Republicans, some of whom have openly criticized the president and his administration in recent months.
"WTF, Steve?" wrote North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis. "Look up the definition of 'humanitarian.' What an embarrassing and outrageous thing to say. You should go back to Ukraine and ask the families of the children Putin has kidnapped and murdered whether they agree your friend Putin is a 'humanitarian.'"
Republican Sen. John Cornyn of Texas responded to a video of Witkoff's comments: "No. Putin is a stone cold killer," he wrote on X.
"Another embarrassment," said Republican Rep. Don Bacon of Nebraska, who has been critical of the Trump administration's handling of Russia and Ukraine.
Republican Sen. Susan Collins of Maine, who has also been critical of the administration, was asked about the comment on the campaign trail and replied, "I would describe Putin as a warmonger, a thug. He's certainly not a humanitarian. He is the aggressor in the war against Ukraine."
Former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine William Taylor, who served during the Bush and Obama administrations, said in an interview with CBS News that it's "absolutely a good thing" Hubbard is coming home, "but he should never have been there in the first place."
"We should not give the Russians any credit for releasing someone who should not have been in jail," Taylor said. "And to call Putin a humanitarian, that's cringeworthy."
Republican Sen. Joni Ernst of Iowa said Putin is "not our friend."
"Vladimir Putin is not our friend, and he is certainly no humanitarian," she posted on X. "His relentless attacks on innocent civilians in Ukraine show his total disregard for human life. Appeasement won't end this war. Pressure will."
Witkoff's praise of Putin also comes as Mr. Trump made the surprise move last week to waive new U.S. sanctions on Russia two days before they were supposed to go into effect, defying Congress and his late friend, Sen. Lindsey Graham. The waivers came one week after Mr. Trump had eased sanctions on Russian diesel and announced a deal with Putin to import diesel to the U.S. market.
Mr. Trump has expressed increasing frustration with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, and on Tuesday, said "Russia, frankly, has been fine on Ukraine. They haven't been doing much."
Before heading to Russia, Witkoff was in Oslo, Norway, where he met with and embraced Zelenskyy. Secretary of State Marco Rubio described that meeting as "positive."

Paris imposes third night of curfew after protest violence
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:55:58 UTC
23:55:58 KST

Paris police have announced a curfew in parts of the French capital for a third consecutive night following violence and looting during nationwide demonstrations.
The restrictions will bar adults and minors from entering designated areas around Place de la Republique and Les Halles from 1100 PM on Wednesday until 0600 AM on Thursday, the Paris police prefecture said on X on Wednesday.
In a separate announcement, the prefecture said gatherings and demonstrations would be banned in certain areas of the capital from 8 PM on Wednesday until 0600 AM on Thursday.
The measures follow instructions from Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu and Interior Minister Laurent Nunez to protect people and property from further violence and looting, the prefecture said.
France has introduced localised curfews in several cities following unrest during October 17 protests against rising living costs and deteriorating conditions in education.
Fresh protests planned
Authorities are preparing for further Yellow Vests demonstrations on Saturday, with Lecornu pledging a “massive” police deployment.
Nunez said security arrangements would be revised to improve police mobility and responsiveness.
Yellow Vests organisers have submitted plans for a march from Place de la Bastille to Place de l’Opera in Paris, although police have yet to confirm the route, according to broadcaster BFMTV.

Russian Navy ship makes another stop on African voyage (VIDEO)
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:55:42 UTC
23:55:42 KST

Russian Navy ship makes another stop on African voyage (VIDEO)
A Russian Navy training ship has arrived in Namibia as part of a voyage around Eurasia and Africa, the Russian Defense Ministry announced on Tuesday. The Baltic Fleet vessel ‘Perekop’ docked at the port of Walvis Bay after crossing the Indian and Atlantic oceans.
According to the ministry, the ship covered more than 1,800 nautical miles in seven days. During the journey, cadets from the Baltic Naval Institute continued their practical training, taking part in navigation watches, plotting courses using onboard instruments, and practicing maneuvers through narrow waterways. They also received instruction in ship operations and damage control.
The vessel was welcomed in Walvis Bay by representatives of the Russian Embassy and the Namibian navу. The visitors who toured the ship were briefed on its operations and the training program for future naval officers. The crew and cadets are also to visit local attractions during their stay.
Earlier in October, ‘Perekop’ called at the port of Maputo, Mozambique’s capital. The vessel also made stops in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania, and Victoria, the capital of Seychelles, in September as part of its ongoing voyage.
According to Sputnik, the voyage is scheduled to conclude on December 9, 2026, after taking the vessel through four oceans, 14 seas, 23 straits, nine bays, and two rivers, with calls at 20 ports, including 12 overseas.
The ‘Perekop’ is not the first Russian naval ship to visit Africa. In July 2025, another Baltic Fleet vessel, the ‘Smolny’, visited the Republic of the Congo as part of a regional tour that also included Equatorial Guinea and São Tomé and Príncipe. The ship had previously called at several African ports in 2024, including in Namibia, Angola, and South Africa.
Russia previously deployed warships to South Africa for joint naval exercises. In January 2026, the Russian Navy’s ‘Stoikiy’ corvette and ‘Yelnya’ tanker took part in the multinational Will for Peace drills off the South African coast.

PHP developers issue updates fixing vulnerabilities that saw websites go offline
- PHP developers released four patches for two critical flaws and urged users to update at once. The bugs could let hackers run code on vulnerable systems.
- PHP Foundation said a researcher found early signs of one flaw in 2024, but it was not fixed sooner. The group called the delay a “structural failure”.
- NSA and CISA warned organisations to patch now or take systems offline. CISA said the flaws had not been exploited yet, but they still pose a risk.
AI generated
BRUSSELS – Developers of the PHP programming language said a set of new updates fixing two previously identified critical vulnerabilities was now live, and acknowledged a delay in addressing a previously identified flaw.
Government websites in Europe and elsewhere went offline on Oct 21 after the disclosure of critical vulnerabilities in PHP sent website operators around the world scrambling to protect their systems.
PHP underpins large parts of the internet and the vulnerabilities had raised concerns that a significant number of websites could be vulnerable to attack. The developers issued four patches to address two “critical” vulnerabilities that could allow hackers to execute code on vulnerable systems.
It said users were strongly encouraged to update immediately.
The PHP Foundation, which oversees development and maintenance of the software, said in a blog post that a security researcher in 2024 found the first signs of a flaw that led to one of the vulnerabilities, and that the issue was “theorised, but no concrete vectors were found, and other concrete issues with clear impact overshadowed these concerns”.
The delay in addressing the flaw “was a structural failure”, the foundation said.
The programming language’s developers had earlier said they had identified two critical vulnerabilities and urged users to update their sites as soon as a fix was released. Security experts warned that hackers would quickly reverse engineer the patches and race to exploit unpatched systems.
The US National Security Agency said in a statement that the vulnerabilities “often provide a direct path to the server’s file system or database”, and that if an immediate update was not feasible, organisations should take systems offline for full mitigation.
The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) said in an advisory that organisations “should immediately update” their PHP installations.
“While CISA has not observed exploitation of these vulnerabilities as of the time of publication, they pose a risk to organisations if left unpatched,” the agency said. REUTERS

'Lefties welcome you': Spain's Sanchez greets Argentine leader with ironic banner
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:50:30 UTC
23:50:30 KST

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez gave Argentine President Javier Milei an ironic welcome to Madrid on Wednesday, proudly embracing the term "leftie" that Milei frequently uses to insult his political opponents.
"Hello, Milei. The lefties welcome you to Spain, the fastest-growing country in Europe," read a large banner displayed outside the headquarters of Sanchez's Socialist Party in Madrid.
Sanchez also posted a video on X responding to Milei's repeated use of the Spanish word "zurdo," or "leftie," as a derogatory term.
"There are those who think they insult us by calling us lefties," he added.
Sanchez added that if raising pensions, increasing the minimum wage yearly, giving parents more time with their children, defending abortion rights and opposing war made someone a leftie, he was proud to be one.
"So yes, I'm a leftie, and proud of it," he concluded.
Milei's visit comes amid longstanding tensions with Sanchez, whom the Argentine president has repeatedly criticised during trips to Spain.
Since taking office in December 2023, Milei has made several visits to Spain without holding official meetings with Sanchez, an unusual pattern that has contributed to diplomatic friction between the two governments.
The latest trip, his seventh to Spain since becoming president, comes ahead of the country's November 29 general election.
The Argentine government has described the visit as part of the election campaign, with Milei seeking to support Spain's right-wing political parties.
However, Milei is not expected to meet far-right Vox leader Santiago Abascal, who is campaigning elsewhere in Spain. Instead, he is scheduled to meet the Vox secretary-general and the director of the party-linked Disenso Foundation.
A possible meeting with Madrid regional President Isabel Diaz Ayuso of the Popular Party, whom he called a "friend" on Wednesday, has yet to be confirmed.
During the visit, Milei also renewed his criticism of Sanchez, calling the Spanish premier an "unpresentable dictator" during a business forum in Madrid on Wednesday.
“When I come to Spain, I'm not going to meet a criminal and a thief like Pedro Sanchez, because I'm not willing to have to sew my pockets shut to avoid being robbed," he added.
Speaking to reporters before the event, Milei also dismissed his critics as "stupid, incompetent, impoverishing lefties."

I&amp;B ministry warns TV channels over communal rhetoric, violent visuals, AI use
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:41:20 UTC
23:41:20 KST

(Representative image): The committee stressed that “inappropriate behaviour or language should not be normalised in telecast”, and urged broadcasters to follow both the letter and spirit of existing rules.
NEW DELHI: Flagging repeated lapses in television content, the information and broadcasting ministry has asked private satellite channels to check communal rhetoric, sensational coverage of crime and violence and the misuse of artificial intelligence in news production, warning that violations of the Programme Code could invite action.In an advisory issued on Wednesday, the ministry said its Inter-Departmental Committee had found content aired by various channels “not in conformity with the spirit of the Programme Code”. It also noted instances of similar news and visuals being broadcast across multiple channels on the same subjects.The committee stressed that “inappropriate behaviour or language should not be normalised in telecast”, and urged broadcasters to follow both the letter and spirit of existing rules.Taking particular note of television debates, the advisory said channels must ensure that discussions do not “promote or encourage communal or anti-national attitudes”. It called for careful selection and prior sensitisation of panellists, adequate editorial control and, where necessary, “immediate remedial measures such as muting, disclaimers, interruption or discontinuation of feed” to stop derogatory, abusive or inflammatory content from being aired.
On AI, the ministry asked broadcasters to exercise caution while using it, including generative tools, for graphics and virtual news presentations. “The use of AI tools may be limited to assistive capacity,” it said, stressing that accuracy, authenticity and sensitivity must not be compromised.The advisory reiterated the prohibition on live coverage of anti-terror operations by security forces, restricting such reporting to periodic briefings by authorised officers. Telecasts of related visuals should be time-stamped wherever necessary to avoid misleading viewers.It also urged channels to avoid graphic or disturbing visuals, unverified and sensationalised crime reports, excessive replay of violent footage and coverage that might glorify unlawful behaviour. Images from disasters and major accidents, it said, should be time-stamped where necessary to prevent panic.
Broadcasters were further reminded to use only authentic maps issued by the Survey of India and protect the identities of sexual offence victims, including through indirect details.The ministry asked channels to strengthen editorial reviews and train news, production and transmission staff in the Programme Code.
Manash Pratim Gohain is a seasoned journalist with over two decades at The Times of India, where he has built a rich body of work spanning education policy, politics, and governance. Renowned for his incisive coverage of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, accreditation reforms, and skilling initiatives, he has also reported on student politics, urban policy, and social movements. His political reportage—both reflective and news-driven—adds depth to his writing, bridging policy with public impact. Through his 2,500 articles and related outlets, he has emerged as a trusted voice in national discourse, particularly in linking education reform to broader societal change.

A new security doctrine for Israel
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:41:02 UTC
23:41:02 KST

A new security doctrine for Israel
MADRID - Israel has a new security doctrine. It has never been published, never presented to the public, and never formally adopted by the military establishment. And yet, since October 7, 2023, it is this unwritten concept, not the doctrine forged over decades, that has shaped Israeli decision-making and now dictates the country’s entire approach to security.
On Monday, Tamir Hayman, former military intelligence chief, set out the principles that, he argued, can be inferred from the policy Israel is actually applying.
The document makes clear that “Jewish identity” must prevail over “its democratic system of government”. This primacy is conceived to guarantee the survival of Israel as a Jewish state, even at the cost of eroding its “democratic values”.
This is nothing new. Modern Zionism was born among the liberal-nationalist currents of nineteenth-century Europe. But unlike the emancipatory nationalisms that sought integration into Europe, Zionism organised a colonisation outwards: a population transfer articulated more as demographic engineering than as an “ancestral return”. Herzl himself considered founding a Jewish state in Argentina or East Africa. Palestine was finally chosen, but the logic was the same: build a homogeneous space for a diaspora. The “return” narrative disguised a colonial settlement project — not merely occupying a land, but displacing and replacing those who inhabited it. The premise became explicit with Vladimir Jabotinsky in The Iron Wall (1923): no Arab people would voluntarily accept being colonised; force was the only way. Therein lies the nucleus of “Greater Israel” — a project that does not contemplate coexistence, but the definitive subordination of the other.
“Democracy” in Israel was established for the Jews after the Zionists expelled 90 percent of the Palestinian population. It makes no sense, then, to speak of “democratic decline”: the foundations on which Israel rests today are racial, and they have always been there for anyone who wished to see them.
Hayman linked this to another principle: security pursued through the establishment of “communities and forward positions in all friction zones with the Arab population, in the occupied West Bank, and in the security zones of Syria, Lebanon and Gaza”.
Under this new approach, aspiring to peace is considered a repetition of the error of the “conceptzia”, the Hebrew label for the strategic assumptions widely blamed for Israel’s failure to foresee the attack of October 7. A meaningful peace agreement in the Middle East is deemed unattainable: peace accords are mere technical, temporary arrangements requiring constant reevaluation. Peace, here, is not an intrinsic value that generates security, but an instrument for other political ends.
“War is necessary, and preventive war is preferable because it allows significant gains from the outset. Its intensity may vary, but its constant presence constitutes an asset for national security,” Hayman wrote. Surprise attacks are the only path to victory; offence takes priority over defence. If Israel cannot withstand a surprise attack or guarantee reliable early warning, the conclusion is foreordained: a standing policy of preventive attacks and preventive wars. This doctrine is no longer hypothetical: Israel applied it in its attacks on Iran in June 2025, and it leaves the door open to future unilateral action.
The document also describes the United States as a “declining power” that “will soon abandon Israel in any case”, and holds that breaking ties with Washington is “essential for Israel’s independence”. Given current social and political shifts in the United States, above all, the majority of the American public’s rejection of the genocide in Gaza, Washington will drop Israel soon regardless, the text concludes.
Arab countries, meanwhile, are treated not as authentic nations but as “collections of tribes and ethnic groups lacking a common history and a foundational national perspective”. Their destabilisation is a natural process, one Israel can manage far more effectively than confronting powerful nation-states, and one it should actively encourage.
The throughline is plain. Israel’s goal has always been to destroy the sovereignty of regioal countries, one after another. Its failure in Iran has forced its strategists to admit they cannot impose their political will everywhere, and to adjust.
On the “Palestinian question”, the document is explicit once more: the solution runs through the deployment of Zionist ideology and its pursuit of the total colonisation of the territory. Hence principled opposition to any political, geographical or security separation between Israel and a Palestinian entity, and to a Palestinian state itself.
Other listed priorities include national arms production, artificial intelligence, quantum computing and the expansion of illegal settlements in the occupied territories.
Israel’s new security doctrine is marked by the current regional landscape, the memory of Hamas’s operation of October 7, and Iran, whose military capacity stands as the symbol of the limit of Israeli power.
Finally, it is worth recalling the roots of Zionism: contrary to what its most obstinate and ignorant defenders claim, it has never been anything but an ideology and a movement of colonial character.

The China-US Quantum Computing Contest
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:40:00 UTC
23:40:00 KST

The Diplomat author Mercy Kuo regularly engages subject-matter experts, policy practitioners, and strategic thinkers across the globe for their diverse insights into U.S. Asia policy. This conversation with Matt Kinsella – the CEO of Infleqtion, a leading U.S. quantum technology company – is the 531st in “The Trans-Pacific View Insight Series.”
Briefly describe U.S. advancements in quantum computing technology.
The United States is moving from experimental quantum systems toward logical, fault-tolerant computing. The key measure is no longer the number of physical qubits, but whether those qubits can be organized into reliable logical qubits and used for meaningful applications.
Infleqtion is at the forefront of that shift. Our neutral-atom platform has demonstrated 12 logical qubits with error detection and loss correction, a 99.73 percent two-qubit gate fidelity, and arrays of up to 1,600 neutral-atom sites. With Nvidia, we published a materials-science demonstration in which logical encoding reduced error approximately sixfold compared with physical-qubit execution.
Our roadmap achieves 30 logical qubits later this year, 100 by 2028, and 1,000 by 2030. We see approximately 100 high-quality logical qubits as the threshold for outperforming classical systems on selected valuable problems.
Hardware alone will not get us there. As our CTO, Pranav Gokhale, has emphasized, hardware-aware software can force-multiply quantum performance. Infleqtion is developing the complete stack – from atoms, photonics, and control systems to error correction, Superstaq compilation, resource estimation, and integration with GPU-accelerated computing. That full-system approach is how quantum computing becomes useful.
In what ways is the U.S. collaborating with partners in the Asia Pacific in developing quantum computing technology?
The United States is building a trusted quantum ecosystem with Asia-Pacific partners through joint research, technology development, workforce training, and access to advanced systems.
Japan provides a strong example. Japan’s Science and Technology Agency selected Infleqtion as the first foreign company – and the only foreign quantum-computing partner – to participate in its Quantum Moonshot program. In a consortium led by Professor Kenji Ohmori of the Institute for Molecular Science, we are contributing neutral-atom technology, photonics expertise, and systems engineering to the development of a large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer based on atomic qubits.
This is more than a research exchange. It combines an American commercial platform with Japanese leadership in ultrafast atomic control and aligns both countries around a shared technical objective. To this end, Infleqtion has delivered neutral-atom systems, helping researchers build the practical experience required to operate and develop applications for advanced quantum machines.
In Australia, Infleqtion has established an Asia-Pacific presence at Swinburne University of Technology and worked with the Australian Army and Australian industry on trustworthy quantum computation. One collaboration with Australian quantum company Diraq explored quantum physically unclonable functions intended to help verify the identity and integrity of remotely accessed quantum computers.
We are also engaging Australian leaders on the future use of quantum computing in energy and infrastructure. This application-led approach is essential: allied programs should begin with consequential problems and jointly determine the hardware, software, and classical resources required to address them.
These partnerships expand the talent, facilities, test environments, and applications available to the United States. Our alliances are not simply diplomatic relationships; they are a practical technology advantage.
Analyze the scope and scale of the U.S.-China quantum computing competition.
The U.S.-China quantum competition is not a single race. It spans computing architecture, logical reliability, software, photonics, manufacturing, talent, supply chains, data-center integration, and applications.
China can concentrate substantial state resources behind selected national programs. The United States operates through a more distributed system of companies, universities, federal laboratories, private capital, and international partners. That diversity supports several technical pathways while creating strong pressure to demonstrate practical results.
Infleqtion represents the strength of the American model. We are advancing a vertically integrated neutral-atom platform while expanding from research milestones into deployed systems and application centers. Our technology is operational in national institutions, and our teams are working with government and industry on energy, materials, AI, and scientific discovery.
We have delivered a 100-physical-qubit system to the U.K. National Quantum Computing Centre, announced a fault-tolerant system for Illinois, opened a Chicago Quantum Innovation Center, and expanded our U.K. engineering and manufacturing presence. These are signs of an industry developing the infrastructure to scale – not merely producing individual experiments.
The competition will be decided by sustained execution: who can build dependable logical systems, reduce resource overhead, manufacture them, connect them to classical supercomputers, and solve consequential problems. The United States has a powerful innovation network, and Infleqtion is rapidly converting that advantage into operating capability.
Examine China’s quantum computing technology developments.
China has demonstrated credible progress in superconducting and photonic quantum computing, supported by centralized programs that coordinate across universities, national laboratories, and state-linked companies. In particular, the University of Science and Technology of China’s Zuchongzhi 3.0 superconducting processor and Jiuzhang 4.0 photonic system have now achieved world-leading results.
These are technically impressive demonstrations, but more consequential questions concern logical error rates, programmable circuit depth, application performance, system availability, and the resources required to outperform the best classical alternative. Of note, China’s leading results in neutral atom quantum computing have lagged developments here in the U.S., though there have been recent accelerations in China’s efforts over the past year.
China is also building domestic control electronics, cloud platforms, software, and industrial capacity. Its 2026-2030 planning framework treats quantum technology as a strategic emerging field, so the United States should expect continued progress.
The appropriate response is disciplined acceleration. We should measure China’s achievements accurately while investing in the capabilities that determine practical advantage: logical qubits, efficient error correction, hardware-aware software, advanced manufacturing, and application deployment. Those are the areas where Infleqtion is concentrating its computing roadmap.
Assess how quantum computing technology is integrated into U.S. national security and defense systems and its implications for the U.S.-China tech race.
Large-scale quantum computers are not yet embedded in operational defense systems. Current integration is occurring through research programs, independent technical validation, hybrid computing infrastructure, and development of mission-relevant applications.
An exemplar is DARPA’s HARQ program exploring heterogeneous systems that combine different quantum processors with classical resources. To meet that demand, Infleqtion is developing Multistaq, a software layer designed to compile and coordinate workloads across multiple qubit technologies.
Infleqtion is also supporting three Department of Energy Genesis Mission projects involving AI-optimized quantum circuits for nuclear applications, fusion research, and deployable atomic sensing. Our planned Illinois system will connect a neutral-atom QPU with Nvidia GPU infrastructure, providing a test environment for quantum-classical workflows and real-time error correction. The associated Chicago center is initially focused on energy-grid and nuclear optimization problems with direct implications for national resilience.
Quantum sensing and timing are closer to field deployment than fault-tolerant computing. Infleqtion’s work in GPS-independent navigation, spectrum awareness, precision timing, gravity sensing, and space systems gives the company operating experience with government missions while strengthening the shared photonics, controls, software, and manufacturing base behind our computers.
For the U.S.-China competition, the objective should be clear: move quantum computing from scientific potential to trusted national infrastructure. Infleqtion is helping the United States do that by combining technical progress, deployed systems, application development, and allied partnerships on one scalable neutral-atom platform.

End of an era? How the Hermes Birkin bag is losing its scarcity appeal
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:39:00 UTC
23:39:00 KST

End of an era? How the Hermes Birkin bag is losing its scarcity appeal
- Hermes Birkin bags are losing resale value as more bags appear online, reducing the profit for resellers like Cai Baochun and Antoinette Hunter.
- The Birkin’s scarcity has driven Hermes’ success, but rising supply, wider resale platforms and softer demand are now putting pressure on its premium image.
- Analysts warn the changing market may weaken Hermes’ business model, even as the company says production depends on trained artisans and quality leather.
AI generated
PARIS/LONDON – London-based Cai Baochun used to make a hefty profit reselling Hermes’ famed Birkin bags for more than double their US$10,000 (S$12,778) retail price. Now he has stopped stockpiling them as second-hand prices fall.
“I don’t want to lose money,” said Cai, who started selling the bags on online platforms such as Vestiaire Collective and on social media in 2020 and rode a Covid-19 pandemic-era luxury spending boom.
The resale value of unworn Birkins sold as second-hand online has dropped by more than US$6,000 from its 2022 peak, he said.
The decline reflects a broader shift in the market for one of luxury’s most exclusive products whose appeal and success have been driven by scarcity.
Increasing supply of Birkin bags in the second-hand market is depressing resale premiums, according to resellers, industry consultants and analysts interviewed by Reuters, raising questions about a strategy that helped propel Hermes to become one of the world’s most profitable luxury companies.
Named after the late British-French actor Jane Birkin, the handbag has been central to Hermes’ performance.
Between 2015 and 2025, group annual sales tripled to €16 billion (S$22.95 billion) while its market value surged.
In 2025, Hermes posted an operating margin of 41%, above that of rivals including Chanel, Kering-owned Gucci and LVMH’s leather and fashion division, which includes Louis Vuitton and Dior.
Resale market under pressure
All of that was underpinned by an aura of exclusivity.
Six resellers who source bags directly from Hermes shoppers said access to a Birkin is generally linked to spending on Hermes scarves, clothes and shoes, although the exact policy differs between regions and stores.
Two estimated customers typically spend US$10,000 to US$20,000 before being offered the Birkin or the Kelly, the brand’s other popular bag.
Hermes, which says a Birkin takes 15 hours to craft, does not disclose its selling policies or how many bags it makes. It declined to comment for this story.
Of the nine Birkin resellers Reuters interviewed in the US, Europe and Asia, six said resale prices had fallen over the past year as more handbags became available, while five reported softer demand.
Antoinette Hunter, who founded luxury handbag reseller Lilac Blue in 2007, said when she got the first request for a Birkin, few people knew the bag.
She eventually sourced one from a member of Japan’s royal family.
Acquiring Birkins is no longer a challenge, Hunter said, but it’s harder to make money from resales.
She said the price for an unworn black Birkin 25 bag, one of the most sought-after models, has fallen by around £4,000 (S$6,842) since 2022, to around £24,000.
Cai, who sells via Vestiaire Collective and Instagram, says his price for the bag is around £20,000.
Hermes sells the same model for £9,390 in Britain, a Hermes sales assistant in London said.
Although Hunter still sees plenty of demand for Hermes bags, particularly the most high-end ones, she said the decline in resale prices might dissuade some from buying directly from Hermes.
“If Hermes continues to raise the prices, and the prices on the resale market continue to drop, that margin gets squeezed, and perhaps it will become less appealing,” she said.
Brokerage Bernstein, which tracks individual auction results, said in a September note the resale price on Birkin 25 bags averaged about 1.7 times the retail tag in the third quarter, down from about 2.6 times at their 2022 peak.
Business model under scrutiny
Hermes’ leather goods division, which includes other handbag models, generates 44% of annual group revenue.
For more than a decade, limited supply and strong demand allowed Birkins to command hefty resale premiums, benefiting both Hermes and resellers as the prospects of making a profit via the secondary market encouraged Hermes clients to buy more from the brand.
“It was a win-win,” said Sarah Davis, founder of California-based Fashionphile.
The company said its Birkin listings have grown 32-fold in 15 years. The company’s website currently lists 212 Birkins on sale.
Hermes has gradually expanded the production of its handcrafted items, opening one workshop per year on average.
Meanwhile, the rise of resale platforms such as Vestiaire Collective and The RealReal, alongside vintage boutiques with online shops and social media channels, has made it easier than ever to resell.
The bags and other Hermes items remain highly sought after, resellers said, but the brand is showing some strain.
Hermes’ shares have lost nearly 40% of their market value in 2026, making the brand one of the worst performers among listed luxury companies.
Earlier in October, UBS analysts downgraded Hermes shares to “sell”, saying that growing secondary-market supply of Birkins and Kellys could weaken the brand’s scarcity-driven business model.
“We believe the nature of the business is changing,” they said in a note, estimating that the number of the handbags listed for sale worldwide is now six to seven times higher than before the Covid-19 pandemic.
The company is expected to report quarterly sales growth of 5.2% on Oct 22, which would mark its weakest quarterly growth in six years, according to Visible Alpha estimates.
While leather goods revenue is still expected to grow by 10%, demand for clothing, silk scarves and perfumes is cooling, a sign fewer customers are making the purchases traditionally required to buy a Birkin at a later stage, two equities analysts and two industry consultants said.
Asked in July whether Hermes should slow production to protect the brand, Hermes CEO Axel Dumas told reporters that some people feared making too many bags would hurt its exclusivity, while others questioned why it was not making more.
He added that output depended largely on the number of fully trained artisans and available high-quality leather.
Not all resellers see weakness.
Davis said prices for the bag on the Fashionphile platform have remained firm and even risen slightly in 2026, pointing to renewed attention generated by Norwegian soccer star Erling Haaland’s handbag collection. REUTERS

Yemen has been engulfed in conflict since the Houthi militia seized Sanaa and several other provinces in September 2014. A Saudi-led coalition intervened in March 2015 in support of the internationally recognised government.

‘Developing trade relations with Africa requires results-oriented economic diplomacy’
TEHRAN- The Advisor to the President for Economic Cooperation, referring to the importance of coordination among government institutions, the private sector, and academic centers, said: “Developing trade relations with Africa requires moving from preliminary and ceremonial talks toward results-oriented economic diplomacy.”
According to IRNA, Masoumeh Aghapour said on Wednesday at the second course of the Iran-Africa Chamber of Commerce, aimed at empowering the younger generation to enter international trade: “To achieve this goal, the government must facilitate the ground for the activity and presence of the private sector; universities and academic centers must provide the necessary knowledge and specialized support; and economic actors, relying on their understanding of the market and their capabilities, must take on the main responsibility for advancing trade projects.”
Aghapour added: “None of these sectors alone can actualize all existing capacities. Cooperation and division of responsibility among the government, universities, and the private sector will pave the way for the formation of an efficient system for developing foreign trade.”
The Advisor to the President for Economic Cooperation, emphasizing the necessity of changing Iran’s approach to developing trade relations with the African continent, said: “Success in African markets will not be achieved by increasing the number of trips and signing memoranda of understanding; rather, we must seek the implementation of real projects, the formation of capable companies, the conclusion of operational contracts, and the training of a new generation of international trade actors.”
He added: “Africa is not merely a market for supplying Iranian goods; it is a strategic horizon for the future of Iran’s economy and an important platform for the effective presence of the new generation in the field of international trade.”
Aghapour, referring to the government’s special attention to the capacities of the younger generation, said: “Belief in the capabilities of young people and their role-playing in the country’s economic transformations is one of the important issues on the path of Iran’s economy transitioning from traditional structures toward a modern economy and broader international interactions.”
He said: “The younger generation, especially young people familiar with modern technologies and global economic developments, can play a role in designing new paths for foreign trade, identifying international opportunities, creating innovative businesses, and developing Iran’s economic relations with other countries.”
The Advisor to the President for Economic Cooperation, referring to the demographic, economic, and trade capacities of the African continent, stated: “Africa, with its young population, broad production and consumption capacities, and developing markets, is one of the important areas for expanding Iran’s economic cooperation. Therefore, the view toward this continent must change from a short-term approach limited to case-by-case interactions to a long-term and targeted strategy.”
He stated: “To effectively exploit these capacities, economic actors’ view of Africa must be based on precise market knowledge, assessment of opportunities, and the design of executive plans. Therefore, success in international markets becomes meaningful when initial contacts lead to sustainable economic cooperation, joint projects, export development, and the creation of added value for the country’s economy.”
Aghapour, referring to the complexities of economic activity in foreign markets, said: “Successful presence in African markets requires precise knowledge of the economic conditions, regulations, and trade mechanisms of destination countries. Before entering any market, economic actors must professionally examine potential risks, the supply chain, laws and regulations, the banking and foreign exchange system, and the methods of conducting trade transactions.”
The Advisor to the President for Economic Cooperation added: “Iranian exporters must carefully study the destination market before offering their products, and by understanding distribution methods, retail shelves, household preferences, and consumer expectations, they must design and offer products suited to market needs.”
Aghapour considered the establishment of a specialized department for trade with Africa and the training of specialized personnel to be among the important steps toward developing economic cooperation with this continent, and stated: “One of the country’s fundamental needs is cultivating human resources familiar with the characteristics of African markets and equipped with specialized knowledge of international trade.”
He added: “Specialized training must be linked with operational experience so that young people can, in addition to becoming familiar with the theoretical foundations of trade, gain experience in real processes of negotiation, marketing, identifying business partners, and implementing contracts.”
The Advisor to the President for Economic Cooperation said: “Developing cooperation with this continent should not be limited to exporting traditional goods; rather, the ground must also be provided for the presence of Iranian technology companies, knowledge-based firms, and providers of specialized services. Therefore, identifying the real needs of destination countries and matching the capabilities of Iranian companies with these needs must be at the center of trade planning.”

Benin, Ghana, Rwanda advance cross-border digital ID pilot
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
22:29:18 CST
23:29:18 KST

KIGALI, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- Benin, Ghana and Rwanda have established initial connectivity to the Smart Africa Data Exchange (SADX), a trusted infrastructure that allows their national systems to securely exchange and verify information, authorities have said.
A statement issued Tuesday in Kigali by the Smart Africa Secretariat said the move marked a key technical milestone in a cross-border digital identity pilot.
Coordinated by the Smart Africa Secretariat, the initiative combines two complementary mechanisms: the Smart Africa Trust Alliance, the common framework of trust, governance and cooperation between participating countries, and the SADX.
Together, they enable cross-border digital interoperability without centralizing identity databases or surrendering control over national data.
The three countries are therefore pioneering a country-led approach to continental digital interoperability, demonstrating how sovereign national systems can progressively establish trusted connections without compromising national control over data, according to the secretariat.
Lacina Kone, chief executive officer of Smart Africa, mentioned that Africa's digital future cannot be built on fragmented national systems.
"Our ambition is to connect our digital economies while preserving the sovereignty of every nation. With Benin, Ghana and Rwanda taking this important first technical step, we are demonstrating that interoperability does not require centralization, and integration does not mean surrendering sovereignty," he said.
The initiative's first use case focuses on cross-border digital identity verification, whereby a traveler from one participating country could have their identity checked directly against their home country's official records, for example at an automated airport e-gate. ■

Interview: World Rowing president confident in beach sprint's Olympic future
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
22:28:59 CST
23:28:59 KST

QINGDAO, China, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- With music playing, waves breaking and athletes sprinting across the sand, the 2026 World Rowing Beach Sprint Finals in Qingdao offered a glimpse of how one of the world's oldest sports is reinventing itself ahead of its Olympic debut at Los Angeles 2028.
For World Rowing President Jean-Christophe Rolland, the event marked an important step in the development of a discipline designed to bring rowing to new audiences through shorter races, unpredictable conditions and a more accessible setting.
In an interview with Xinhua during the competition, Rolland discussed beach sprint rowing's growing appeal, preparations for its Olympic debut and China's increasingly prominent role in the sport.
STILL ROWING, "BUT COMPLETELY DIFFERENT"
Beach sprint is a short, head-to-head knockout format of coastal rowing, the open-water branch of the rowing family.
While classic rowing takes place on flat water with specialized boats, coastal rowing is raced at sea where waves demand sturdier craft. Beach sprint adds a third dimension: athletes start by running on the beach, jump into their boats, race through two 250-meter sections around buoys and sprint back across the sand to hit the finish button.
"It is still rowing because we have a boat, a sliding seat and oars. But the concept, the environment and the rules are completely different," he said.
That difference, he argued, is exactly its appeal. Music, the beach setting, running on sand and jumping into the boat make it "a little more fun," while the waves inject an element of uncertainty.
"Depending on how athletes ride the waves, they are affected by the surrounding conditions. That makes the sport a little unpredictable. For the public and spectators, it is probably more fun and faster-paced."
He also drew a clear line between the two coastal formats held in Qingdao: last week's World Rowing Coastal Championships is a six-kilometer endurance race with all crews starting together, while beach sprint is a compact knockout competition, the exact format that will appear at the Los Angeles Olympics.
READY FOR THE OLYMPIC STAGE
Rowing has been part of the Olympic program since the first modern Games in 1896, while coastal rowing only took shape about two decades ago. In October 2023, the IOC Executive Board approved coastal rowing beach sprints for LA 2028, where men's solo, women's solo and mixed double sculls will award three sets of medals.
"It allows us to reach different territories and different audiences, and the environment is completely different from classic rowing," Rolland said. "At the Olympic Games, we can benefit from sharing a venue with other sports rather than needing a standalone venue."
With two years to go, he said the discipline is still maturing. "When the discipline started, it was limited to a very small number of countries. Now its inclusion in the Olympic program has encouraged countries to invest in it. I would not say that we have reached maturity yet, but it is absolutely clear that this discipline really matters in rowing. It continues to grow year after year."
World Rowing is refining the rules to keep them simple. A World Beach Sprint Series will be launched in 2027, with stops in Türkiye and China.
Rolland called the Qingdao finals "a key milestone" on the road to the Olympics. "They allow us to keep improving the event and to show that we have reached the Olympic standard, both in the product we deliver and in the quality and performance of the athletes."
CHINA, "A VERY ACTIVE CONTRIBUTOR"
This was Rolland's first visit to Qingdao, a city known worldwide for its beer. "But there is much more to the city than beer," he said, "The athletes from around the world who are here are very pleased and happy, because we have a very good environment for these world championships."
His bond with China dates back nearly 30 years, to when he first visited as an athlete after the Atlanta Games. "Since then, I have seen the incredible development of rowing in the country," he said, citing the support of the water sports administration and the Chinese Rowing Association, which he described as "one of the most contributive member federations worldwide."
In 2025, China hosted the World Rowing Championships for the first time in Shanghai, followed by the Shanghai Sprint, the coastal championships and now the beach sprint finals. "This shows how active China has become in rowing and how much it contributes to the sport."
He recalled China's women's rowing medals at the Tokyo Olympics and his visit to China's National Games last year, where he was impressed by young athletes. "China has a large number of athletes and the capacity to perform at the highest level," he said.
For China's young rowers, his advice was simple: "Train, train, train. There is no other path to performance than training and making the effort."
"Sport is about respect, respecting one another, respecting the rules and doing your very best to perform," he said. "There is also friendship and the relationships we build with other athletes. We are a family. Competition is competition, but we can still create very good relationships among athletes." ■

National Export Day ceremony held with President Pezeshkian in attendance
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
14:28:54 UTC
23:28:54 KST

National Export Day ceremony held with President Pezeshkian in attendance
TEHRAN- The National Export Day ceremony was held on Wednesday morning, October 21, at the Summit Hall, with the attendance of President Masoud Pezeshkian; Foreign Affairs Minister Abbas Araghchi; Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade Seyed Mohammad Atabak; Head of the Trade Promotion Organization Mohammad Ali Dehghan Dehnavi; Head of the Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines, and Agriculture Samad Hassanzadeh; those active in the field of foreign trade, and related experts, to honor national exemplary exporters.
At the 30th National Export Day ceremony, the Export Atlas system was unveiled, and 13 national premium companies and 43 national exemplary companies were honored.
A joint committee should be formed to quickly remove export barriers
The Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade, emphasizing the need to accelerate the removal of export barriers, called for the formation of a joint committee with the participation of the Iran Chamber of Commerce, the Ministry of Industry, Mining and Trade, and the Central Bank to quickly resolve exporters’ problems.
Seyed Mohammad Atabak, Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade, speaking at the National Export Day ceremony and referring to the presence of private-sector representatives in the Supreme Council for Non-Oil Exports, stated: “Given the multiplicity of government bodies present in this council, it is necessary to form a specialized committee before issues are raised at the highest level, so that the required matters are examined there and, as far as possible, decided.”
Addressing the President, the Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade added: “In the current situation, especially given hour-by-hour changes in the status of some borders, decisions must be made more quickly. Accordingly, I propose that a committee be formed with the membership of the Iran Chamber of Commerce, the Ministry of Industry, Mining and Trade, and the Central Bank so that it can decide on the current issues and problems of exporters. In cases requiring decision-making at a higher level, the approvals of this working group would be submitted to the Supreme Council for Non-Oil Exports for final approval.”
Atabak, referring to the unveiling of the comprehensive atlas of the country’s official foreign trade gateways at the ceremony, said: “It is expected that this atlas will become a reference for foreign trade actors. Of course, to maintain its effectiveness, the information must be continuously updated, and this can be pursued under the stewardship of the Trade Promotion Organization of Iran.”
He also emphasized the need to strengthen the presence of Iranian traders in target markets and referred to the capacities of the country’s trade agreements, saying: “In some markets, including the Eurasian Economic Union, there are fewer barriers to trade development, but the presence of Iranian traders in these markets still needs strengthening.”
The Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade, referring to last week’s meeting with officials of the Eurasian Economic Union, stated: “At this meeting, the Union’s officials did not consider the number of Iranian traders active in the Union’s market to be proportionate to existing capacities. This is while the efforts of the country’s exporters have placed Iran among the top countries in this field; nevertheless, increasing the presence of Iranian traders in the markets of member states remains necessary.”
Atabak also announced agreements in the field of standards and said: “It was agreed that, to prevent export stoppages due to standards issues, the country’s prevailing standards and certificates of origin would be used so that the export process continues and exported goods do not face stoppage due to these barriers.”
He emphasized the need to follow up on the agreements made, continuously update the comprehensive atlas of the country’s official foreign trade gateways, and strengthen decision-making mechanisms to remove export barriers.
Drafting of 10 proposals to remove trade barriers and develop value-creating exports / Necessity of compensating for increased transportation costs
The Head of the Trade Promotion Organization of Iran, while emphasizing the need to facilitate regulations, compensate for increased transportation costs, and strengthen the presence of Iranian firms in global markets, announced the drafting of 10 proposals aimed at entering the decision-making cycle and facilitating the path of exporters’ activity.
Mohammad Ali Dehghan Dehnavi, at the 30th National Export Day ceremony, emphasized the necessity of supporting exporters, removing domestic barriers, and strengthening the infrastructure for export development.
Dehghan Dehnavi, referring to the position of exporters in the country’s economy, said: “National Export Day is not a day for stating numbers and lists of actions; rather, it is a day to appreciate those who have created and maintained a link between the domestic market and foreign customers.”
He added that exporters did not stop the trade process under the difficult conditions caused by war, sanctions, and economic blockade: “Despite problems in transferring funds, exporters remained committed to their obligations and worked to sustain employment. This resilience demonstrates their decisive role in maintaining the flow of trade and the continuity of the country’s economic activities.”
The Head of the Trade Promotion Organization of Iran, referring to the slogan “Dynamic Trade, Value-Creating Exports,” stated: “This year’s slogan cannot be reduced to a mere title; rather, it is a criterion for measuring the performance of actors in the non-oil export field.”
The Head of the Trade Promotion Organization of Iran, referring to the importance of transportation routes in the country’s foreign trade, stated: “Seventy-five percent of the country’s foreign trade was conducted via sea, but with the efforts of various agencies, especially the private sector, we were able to redefine alternative routes during this period and continue the trade process.”
Dehghan Dehnavi, emphasizing Iran’s capacities for trade development, added: “The country possesses capabilities, knowledge, skills, and specialized human resources that can be used to increase trade volume and raise it from one billion dollars a week to one billion dollars a day.”
The Deputy Minister of Industry, Mining and Trade called exporters the front line of the economic war and stated: “It is our duty to remove the domestic barriers facing exporters and facilitate the path of exporters’ activity.”
Dehghan Dehnavi, referring to the increase in transportation costs under current conditions, considered the allocation of appropriate incentives to be one of the solutions for compensating for the increased costs and said: “We must remove the existing barriers in the path of trade, facilitate regulations, and develop the necessary executive capacities for the effective presence of economic actors in global markets.”
He further stated, emphasizing the preservation of target markets and the achievement of value-creating exports: “Exporters have guaranteed the sustainability of the country’s trade despite numerous pressures. On this path, we must, by strengthening export capacities and focusing on creating added value, provide the ground for a more sustainable presence of Iranian products and services in global markets.”
The Head of the Trade Promotion Organization of Iran also emphasized the necessity of making solution-oriented decisions and announced the drafting of 10 proposals, expressing hope that by placing these proposals in the decision-making cycle, the process of addressing issues and removing barriers to export development would be accelerated.
Dehghan Dehnavi, in conclusion, expressed gratitude for the efforts of economic actors and those involved in the country’s export development.
Iran Chamber president urges unified, programmatic trade strategy to counter external pressure
Speaking at the same ceremony, Iran Chamber of Commerce, Industries, Mines and Agriculture (ICCIMA) President Samad Hassanzadeh praised exporters for maintaining export flows despite difficult economic and wartime conditions and for resisting enemy intentions. He said protecting exports during the recent critical war conditions was a strategic necessity for employment, foreign-exchange earnings, and Iran’s economic credibility, and commended the Ministry of Industry, Mining and Trade, the Trade Promotion Organization, and other agencies for pursuing barriers and supporting trade routes.
Hassanzadeh said Iran remains in a “neither war, nor peace” situation marked by uncertainty, economic pressure, trade restrictions, and threats to transport routes. Foreign trade is increasingly affected, and the enemy seeks to weaken Iran’s economic competitiveness by raising transaction costs. The response, he argued, must be a unified message from government officials and the private sector: turn external pressure into a coherent will to keep trade flowing, remove domestic barriers, and neutralize the cost of foreign pressure through rationality, pragmatism, and decisions based on national interests.
He called for moving from day-to-day crisis management to sustainable trade mechanisms and for redefining export’s place in macro-economic policy. This requires coordination among foreign-exchange, industrial, financial, and trade policies and avoiding decisions that raise the cost of Iranian firms’ presence in markets. He proposed a Foreign Trade Continuity Headquarters, with government and private-sector participation, customs, the Central Bank, and other agencies, to draft an operational plan. Priorities included diversifying transport routes, easing customs and border procedures, strengthening trade insurance and risk management, and improving inter-agency coordination.
On forex policy, Hassanzadeh urged aligning currency-repatriation and working-capital mechanisms with trade realities. He called for reviewing restrictive business-card procedures, distinguishing intentional violations from limited and recoverable obligations, giving proportionate time to meet foreign-exchange commitments, and avoiding punitive measures against reputable exporters.
He stressed that preserving traditional markets and developing new ones requires attention to costs, payment terms, tariffs, and freight. Without logical support, Iranian exporters cannot compete with regional and international rivals, and lost markets are not easily regained. He urged making economic diplomacy operational—pursuing tariff and transport agreements, removing customs obstacles, and expanding cooperation with neighbors, with greater coordination between relevant agencies, ICCIMA, and joint chambers.
Finally, Hassanzadeh called for moving from sporadic exports to sustainable market presence through value added, quality, completed production chains, and stronger Iranian brands, while supporting downstream industries, technical and engineering services, knowledge-based products, and service exports. He also urged redefining government–private sector relations based on trust, partnership, and responsibility, and turning private-sector demands into a prioritized, time-bound action plan.

Uganda's economy shows resilience amid global shocks: ministry
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
22:28:53 CST
23:28:53 KST

KAMPALA, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- Uganda's economy continues to show resilience amid global economic shocks and geopolitical uncertainties, the Ministry of Finance, Planning and Economic Development said Wednesday.
The ministry's Performance of the Economy Report for September 2026 said high-frequency indicators of economic activity and business sentiment pointed to continued economic growth, with output and demand improving since the start of the 2026/27 financial year on July 1.
The Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) stood at 53.0 in September, above the 50-point threshold that separates expansion from contraction. The reading indicated improving private-sector business conditions, as firms continued to report increased output and new orders amid sustained customer demand, the report said.
The Composite Index of Economic Activity rose by 0.3 percent to 193.87 in August from 193.30 in July, reflecting an increase in economic activity over the previous month.
Business sentiment also remained positive, with the Business Tendency Index reaching 55.80 in September, above the 50-point threshold.
However, annual headline inflation rose to 4.6 percent in the year to September, up from 4.1 percent in the year to August, according to the report. The increase reflected higher prices across various categories of goods and services, driven by unfavorable weather conditions that affected food crop supplies. Higher transportation and energy costs, amid continued increases in international oil prices, further pushed up production costs.
Uganda's trade deficit with the rest of the world also widened by 151 percent to 817.03 million U.S. dollars in August 2026, from 325.53 million dollars in the same month of 2025.
The government is undertaking various initiatives to reverse this trend, including enhancing economic and commercial diplomacy through facilitating our missions and embassies abroad to promote our exports and tourism attractions while also sourcing investments into the economy, prioritizing value addition to export products through agro-processing and mineral development, the report said. ■

The premiere of the documentary film "The Elephant Odyssey", which follows the improbable journey of the wandering Asian elephants in southwest China's Yunnan Province that captivated viewers around the world, was held in Beijing on Wednesday.

China's economic powerhouse province steps up integration of AI, IP protection

23:28:50 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- East China's economic powerhouse Jiangsu Province on Wednesday outlined efforts to integrate artificial intelligence (AI) and intellectual property (IP) protection, aiming to foster innovation and improve efficiency.
According to provincial IP authorities, Jiangsu has 68,000 invention patents in the AI sector. By 2025, the province had 292,000 high-value invention patents, accounting for 12.7 percent of China's national total.
Jiangsu has strengthened IP protection for AI research and businesses. IP protection centers across the province have established expedited pre-examination procedures for AI patent applications, reducing the average approval time from 22 months to just three months. It has also issued guidelines to help AI companies operated by one person, or OPCs, comply with IP-related requirements.
Meanwhile, Jiangsu is applying AI to improve IP services. It has developed AI infrastructure, such as a digital innovation laboratory, and created AI models and application scenarios to boost the efficiency of IP-related work.
"We should both make good use of AI as a powerful tool and provide institutional support for the development of the AI industry," said Zhang Chuanbo, a senior provincial IP official, at a press conference held by the China National Intellectual Property Administration (CNIPA) in Beijing.
Jiangsu has long been a major manufacturing and foreign trade hub in China, while several of its cities have emerged as centers of technological innovation. Suzhou, Nanjing and Zhenjiang were included in the World Intellectual Property Organization's ranking of the top 100 innovation clusters this year.
The 15th China International Patent Fair will be held in Jiangsu's Wuxi in November, according to the CNIPA. ■

China adds 1,625 km of new rail lines amid push to build modern railway infrastructure
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
22:28:47 CST
23:28:47 KST

BEIJING, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- China put a total of 1,625 kilometers of new railway lines into operation in the first three quarters of 2026 as the country, home to the world's largest high-speed rail network, speeds up efforts to build a modern railway infrastructure system.
During the period, the railway sector completed fixed-asset investment of 601.2 billion yuan (about 89 billion U.S. dollars), up 1.3 percent year on year, according to data from the China State Railway Group Co., Ltd. (China Railway).
With the newly opened lines and continuing investment, the overall efficiency of the railway network has continued to improve and new momentum has been injected into economic and social development, the company said.
During the period, a number of new lines and stations were put into operation. On Sept. 28 this year, China opened four high-speed rail sections, connecting Xiongan in north China's Hebei Province with Shangqiu in Henan Province in central China, Xi'an with Ankang in Shaanxi Province in northwest China, Yichang with Xingshan in central China's Hubei Province, and Harbin with Yichun in Heilongjiang Province in the country's northeast.
"These projects have further optimized regional railway networks, improved overall transport efficiency, and made travel more convenient for people along the routes," the company said, adding that they have also driven industrial upgrading and resource development, becoming a new engine for high-quality regional economic and social development.
By the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, which included more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, featuring eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones across the country.
Continued investment in the sector reflects the growing demand for railway travel in the world's second-largest economy.
Railway passenger trips hit a record high in the first three quarters in the country, totaling 3.71 billion passenger trips in the period, up 4.8 percent year on year, China Railway data showed.
Earlier this month, the National Railway Administration released a plan that proposes to basically establish a science and technology innovation system that leads railway modernization by 2030.
The plan envisions no fewer than 20 typical application scenarios or demonstration projects in areas such as the 400 km/h high-speed train operating system. Regarding technical equipment, it proposes to advance research on 600 km/h high-speed maglev technology as well as testing and verification of key technologies for domestic production. ■

====================================================================================================

Africa faces most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak on record as DR Congo cases near 10,000
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-10-21
22:28:35 CST
23:28:35 KST

KINSHASA, Oct. 21 (Xinhua) -- Africa is grappling with "the most geographically widespread Ebola outbreak in history", according to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC), as infections in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) approach 10,000 and newly reported cases in Kenya and Nigeria raise concerns over the virus's spread across borders.
Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya warned Tuesday that the outbreak had already affected multiple countries across three regions of Africa, calling for urgent international support to contain further transmission.
Nearly five months after the outbreak was declared in the DRC, the epidemic has claimed more than 4,600 lives in the country and spread to eight of its 26 provinces, while imported infections have exposed vulnerabilities in cross-border disease surveillance.
CROSS-BORDER SPREAD RAISES ALARM
Nigeria on Tuesday confirmed its first case of Ebola caused by the Bundibugyo virus, the same strain responsible for the ongoing epidemic in the DRC, becoming the fifth country to detect the virus since the outbreak began in May, according to the Nigerian health authorities.
The patient, a woman who had recently traveled through Uganda, developed symptoms on Oct. 7 and sought medical care at a private hospital in Abuja four days later. Her infection was confirmed on Oct. 20. Nigerian authorities have identified 44 contacts for monitoring, while the patient remains in isolation and is receiving medical care.
Uganda's Ministry of Health said the woman had traveled to eastern DRC for business before transiting through Uganda in early October without symptoms. It stressed that her travel through Uganda did not establish where she contracted the virus, with investigations still underway.
Uganda, which previously reported 20 confirmed Ebola cases and two deaths linked to the DRC outbreak, was declared Ebola-free on Aug. 27 after completing a 42-day monitoring period without new infections.
The ministry reiterated Tuesday that Uganda still had "no confirmed active Ebola cases" and pledged to strengthen health screening and surveillance at points of entry.
Meanwhile, Kenya reported its ninth confirmed Ebola case on Tuesday, with all infections linked to an initial imported case involving a Kenyan national who had traveled from the DRC through Uganda and died in Nairobi on Oct. 5.
The latest patient was already in quarantine when symptoms developed. Kenyan health authorities said there was no evidence of transmission beyond the identified cluster, while 134 of 135 identified contacts had been placed under quarantine.
DR CONGO OUTBREAK NEARS GRIM MILESTONE
In the DRC, the outbreak continues to take a heavy toll despite signs of slowing transmission in some areas.
The country had recorded 9,637 confirmed cases and 4,646 deaths as of Oct. 19, representing a case fatality rate of 48.2 percent, according to the latest situation report released Wednesday by the country's health authorities.
The eastern province of Ituri remains the epicenter, accounting for 72.7 percent of cumulative infections. Neighboring North Kivu has also emerged as a major transmission hotspot, recording 2,117 confirmed cases and 1,191 deaths, with a case fatality rate of 56.3 percent.
The virus has also recently reached the northern province of Nord-Ubangi, bringing the number of affected provinces to eight and the number of affected health zones to 66.
The outbreak's geographical expansion has also raised concerns over the risk of the virus reaching Kinshasa, the country's densely populated capital of nearly 20 million people.
Former health minister Jean-Jacques Mbungani Mbanda warned Tuesday that the detection of infections in the northern provinces of Sud-Ubangi and Nord-Ubangi had heightened the risk of imported cases reaching the capital through river transport, air travel and road networks.
He urged authorities to strengthen surveillance at airports, river ports and other entry points, warning that temperature screening alone could not identify infected travelers during the incubation period.
Mbungani also called for stronger community surveillance and infection prevention measures in healthcare facilities, stressing that Kinshasa should reinforce its preparedness before recording its first confirmed case.
AFRICA CDC CALLS FOR URGENT GLOBAL ACTION
Africa CDC Director-General Jean Kaseya warned Tuesday that the continued geographical spread of the outbreak, coupled with a case fatality rate approaching 50 percent in the DRC, posed an extremely serious public health threat.
In a statement following Nigeria's confirmation of its first case, Kaseya said Africa CDC has begun mobilizing support for Nigeria while intensifying its response in the DRC and Kenya and maintaining heightened vigilance in Uganda.
Calling for urgent international support, Kaseya appealed for flexible financing, medical supplies, diagnostic tools, trained responders and stronger community-based surveillance.
"We cannot allow this outbreak to spread to more countries or continue for another year," he warned.
WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus also called for sustained regional preparedness following Nigeria's confirmation of its first Bundibugyo Ebola case.
In a social media statement Wednesday, Tedros urged countries across the region to maintain a high level of readiness to detect cases early, prevent further transmission and protect healthcare workers and communities.
The outbreak is caused by Bundibugyo virus, for which no vaccine or specific treatment has yet been approved, making early detection, supportive care and effective infection control crucial to reducing deaths and interrupting transmission.
The epidemic was declared in the DRC on May 15 and designated a public health emergency of international concern by WHO two days later. Africa CDC subsequently declared it a public health emergency of continental security.
The current Ebola outbreak has become the largest and deadliest ever recorded in the DRC and the second-largest Ebola outbreak globally, after the 2014-2016 West Africa epidemic. ■
